title: Health Care Assistant
company: Atlas Care Homes Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Healthcare Assistant to join our team at Rosewood House. The successful candidate will provide essential support to patients and residents within care homes and home care settings. This role involves assisting with daily activities, ensuring the well-being of individuals, and supporting the delivery of personalised care plans. The position offers an opportunity to make a meaningful difference in people's lives while working within a professional and caring environment.

Responsibilities

Assist patients and residents with personal care tasks such as bathing, dressing, and mobility.

Support individuals with their daily routines, including meal preparation and medication reminders.

Maintain accurate records of care provided in accordance with care plans.

Communicate effectively with patients, families, and healthcare professionals to ensure high standards of care.

Drive between different care settings or appointments as required, ensuring timely attendance.

Assist with light domestic duties to promote a clean and safe environment.

Follow all health and safety protocols to ensure the safety of both patients and staff.

Participate in ongoing training programmes to stay updated on best practices in healthcare assistance.

title: Female Enabling Support Worker
description:
Female Enabling Support Worker

Location: Newcastle

Salary: £13.45 per hour

Hours: 40 hours per week

Are you the Enabling Support Worker We re Looking For?

Do you have a passion for supporting people with complex needs to live fulfilling, independent lives? Are you an experienced care professional ready to take the next step in your career?

At Shaftesbury North East, we're looking for dedicated and motivated Enabling Support Workers to join our Complex Care Service. We are looking for someone with a sense of fun, to help make a real difference to the lives of the people we support every day. Knowledge of the local area would be advantageous.

Due to service requirements, only Female applicants will be considered. A full UK license is required. Please note that we are not currently offering Sponsorship for this role.

About You

To be successful in this role, you'll have:
- A minimum of 12 months' experience supporting people with complex needs, learning disabilities, autism, and behaviours of concern within a supported living environment.
- NVQ/QCF level 2 or a desire to work towards the qualification while working
- A person-centred approach and a genuine passion for delivering outstanding support.

About the Role

As a Enabling Support Worker it will be your role to provide support and encouragement, by taking direction from both the person supported and the person centred support plan.

You will be required to maintain accurate records while at work, in line with the service requirements. You may also be required to administer personal care and medication.

There may be a requirement to cover sleep in sessions. You will be paid an additional £60 per sleep in.

Benefits of working at Shaftesbury

At Shaftesbury, we know that our workers are our greatest asset. We re proud to have some of the best and most committed staff in the sector and we want to attract more people like you to work with Shaftesbury. We re now offering even more great benefits to reward the work of our wonderful staff, which is listed below:
- Happy Birthday to you! As well as sending you a birthday card, all frontline care staff can have the opportunity to take the day off on their birthday, taken from your annual entitlement.
- Great CQC, great reward. If your service is rated good or equivalent by CQC in all domains, all staff will receive a £30 gift voucher. If rated outstanding, all staff will receive a £50 gift voucher.
- We want to reward staff in a range of ways for their hard work. You can be nominated for a recognition letter from a member of the Executive Leadership Team and you may also be nominated to receive a gift voucher up to £50 for going above and beyond within your role.
- Excellent training package provided for all staff.
- Generous Annual Leave entitlement of 25 days + 8 days bank holiday for the first 5 years. Increasing to 28 days + 8 days bank holiday after 5 years.
- Pension Scheme.
- Access to our employee assistance program.

Shaftesbury is the disability charity that s committed to enabling children, young people and adults to live a life that adds up for them.

What makes life liveable is never down to just one thing - it s the sum of many things. From friendship to fun; from companionship to community; from a great chat to a challenge overcome, it all adds up to Shaftesbury.

Through a wide range of disability care, special education, and rehabilitation services we promote inclusion and wellbeing for all. Together, we work to see people take part, contribute and be valued. We put the elements in place that all add up to connected lives.

Shaftesbury is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable children and adults and expects all employees to share this commitment. All offers of employment are subject to an enhanced DBS/Access NI check.

Shaftesbury is committed to the Disability Confident Scheme and to equal opportunities therefore we welcome and encourage applications from everyone regardless of age, disability, gender, ethnicity, religion and sexual orientation.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Shaftesbury Group, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

title: Care Assistant - Care Home
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Care Assistant at Barchester, you'll play a vital role in helping our residents enjoy each day to the fullest. Providing both practical support and meaningful companionship, you'll make a genuine difference to the lives of the people you care for.

In this role, you'll:
- Support residents with daily living activities and personal care
- Help residents with food and drink throughout the day
- Build positive relationships and provide companionship
- Follow individual care plans and support resident wellbeing
- Spend valuable one-to-one time with residents
- Encourage independence while promoting dignity and respect
- Work as part of a caring team to deliver high-quality support

No two days are ever the same, making this a rewarding opportunity to use your skills, develop your experience and make a real impact every day.

ABOUT YOU

We're looking for someone who is kind, compassionate and committed to delivering excellent care.

To join us as a Care Assistant, you'll have:
- Experience caring for older people
- A positive, can-do attitude
- Excellent communication and people skills
- A warm, empathetic and respectful approach
- A genuine passion for supporting others

Above all, you'll have the compassion and dedication needed to provide the highest standard of care and support. In return, we'll give you all the training and development you need to succeed.

REWARDS PACKAGE

In return for your dedication, you'll receive a competitive rate of pay plus a sector-leading benefits and rewards package, including:
- Free training and development opportunities
- Access to wellbeing and support tools
- A range of retail discounts and savings
- Unlimited referrals through our Refer a Friend bonus scheme
- Employee of the Month recognition
- Long Service Awards
- Career development opportunities within one of the UK's leading care providers

And so much more!

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality of care you'd expect for your own loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

Our Care Home Manager is always happy to welcome you into the home for an informal chat, so feel free to pop in and find out more about working at Barchester.

title: Care Assistant
company: North Haven Care and Support Ltd - Agency - Permanent
salary_text: £14.44 - £14.94 per hour (extra 35p per mile for driving roles)
description:
Job Title: Care Assistants

Location: South Shields, South Tyneside

Salary: 14.44 - 14.94 per hour + 35p per mile for driving roles

Job Type: Permanent - Full Time, Part Time or Casual (guaranteed hours available)

No care experience? No problem. We'll give you full paid training, two paid shadow shifts and a fully funded Social Care diploma, so all you need to bring is a passion for helping others.

About us:

North Haven Care and Support Ltd is a Good CQC rated home care provider across South Tyneside and Sunderland. We help people with a wide range of conditions stay independent, stay in control of their own lives and stay in the homes they love.

About the role:

As a Care Assistant, you'll visit clients in their own homes and out in the local community, helping them live well and keeping their pride and dignity. No two days are the same. You'll help with:
- Personal care
- Preparing meals
- Administering medicine
- Shopping and household tasks

We have a number of positions available and are recruiting for two types of role:
- Driving carers (3-4 roles): you'll need a full licence and access to a vehicle, with mileage paid at 35p per mile
- Walking carers (2-3 roles): no licence needed, as you'll cover clients within walking distance of each other

Shifts: Earlies (7am-3pm) and/or lates (3pm-11pm) on a rota, with some weekends. Choose the hours that fit around childcare, study or other commitments.

Areas covered: Marsden, Whitburn, Cleadon, The Nook, Simonside, West Harton, Brockley Whins, Westoe, West Park and Tyne Dock.

About you:
- You're caring, compassionate and a good listener
- You enjoy building relationships with a diverse range of individuals
- You can drive and have access to a vehicle (preferred)
- Experience is welcome but not required. Experienced carers with an up-to-date DBS check can start quickly

What we offer:
- Up to 14.94 per hour, plus 35p per mile for driving roles
- 28 days' annual leave (pro rata)
- Paid classroom training and paid shadow shifts
- Fully funded QCF diploma in Social Care and a clear route to progress
- Flexible hours and guaranteed hours contracts
- Pension scheme
- Free on-site parking
- Referral programme

Additional Information:

All successful candidates will need an enhanced DBS check.

If this sounds like the ideal opportunity for you just click on the APPLY button, we look forward to hearing from you!

Candidates with experience of; Care Assistant, Carer, Home Carer, Care Worker, Domiciliary Care Worker, Domiciliary Carer, Support Worker, Community Care Worker, Healthcare Assistant, Personal Care Assistant, Home Care Assistant, Social Care Worker will also be considered for this role.

title: Children Support Worker
description:
Residential Support Worker - Make a Real Difference Every Day

Are you passionate about supporting children and young people to achieve positive outcomes? Do you want a rewarding career where you can make a genuine difference in a child's life?

We are recruiting on behalf of a specialist residential childcare provider for a Residential Support Worker to join a dedicated team in Sunderland. This is an excellent opportunity for caring, resilient and motivated individuals looking to develop a career within residential childcare, children's services, support work, youth work or social care.

Whether you already have experience working with children and young people or are looking to take the next step into the sector, we'd love to hear from you.

The Role

As a Residential Support Worker, you will provide high-quality care and support to children and young people living in a residential home setting. You will help create a safe, stable and nurturing environment while promoting independence, personal growth and emotional wellbeing.

Key Responsibilities
- Supporting children and young people with daily routines, education and activities
- Building positive, trusting and professional relationships
- Encouraging independence, confidence and essential life skills
- Promoting emotional wellbeing and positive behaviour
- Creating a safe, caring and supportive home environment
- Working collaboratively with colleagues, families, social workers and external agencies
- Following safeguarding policies, procedures and children's care plans
- Maintaining accurate records, reports and documentation
- Supporting young people to achieve personal goals and outcomes

About You

We are looking for individuals who are:
- Caring, compassionate and committed to making a difference
- Resilient and able to remain calm in challenging situations
- Strong communicators with excellent interpersonal skills
- Reliable, professional and able to work effectively as part of a team
- Flexible to work shifts, weekends and sleep-ins
- Passionate about supporting vulnerable children and young people

Desired Experience

A relevant qualification in Health & Social Care, Children & Young People's Workforce or Residential Childcare is desirable but not essential.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive pay of £13.50 per hour
- Comprehensive induction and ongoing training
- Career development and progression opportunities
- Supportive and experienced management team
- Rewarding work with real purpose and impact
- Opportunity to build a long-term career within children's residential care

Apply Today

If you're looking for a rewarding Residential Support Worker job in Sunderland, and want to help children and young people thrive in a safe and supportive environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now for immediate consideration and take the next step in your residential childcare career.

title: Regional Care Assistant
description:
A 500 'Golden Hello' Welcome Bonus is just one of the ways we'll reward you when you join Barchester in this role.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Regional Care Assistant with Barchester care homes, you'll deliver warm, empathetic and respectful care and support across a 20-mile radius to help our residents get the most out of life. On a practical level, you can expect to monitor the delivery of care when on duty, contribute to the person-centred care planning process for each resident and record observations on things like temperature and blood pressure amongst a range of other important tasks. The role of Regional Care Assistant is very varied and also involves providing support and companionship. It's vital for us that every resident enjoys meaningful one-to-one time with our carers, every single shift.

ABOUT YOU
A background in care is important for the role of Regional Care Assistant, and you'll need a good understanding of elderly care. A Level 2 NVQ in Health & Social Care would be useful, as would a good understanding of the wider healthcare industry. Ideally, you'll also have a C or above in GCSE English and Maths. Dedicated and compassionate, your passion for people means you'll go above and beyond to support the wellbeing of residents. Because you'll be travelling across the area, you'll either need your own car or ready access to one. We'll cover your mileage when you travel over five miles from your main home, and if you're on duty at the time of an inspection and we achieve a Good' rating, you'll qualify for a bonus.

title: Young People Support Worker
description:
Young People Support Worker

We are seeking compassionate and motivated Support Workers to help young people in Durham build confidence, develop skills and move towards independence.

Position: Young People Support Worker and Night Young People Support Worker
Salary: £26,436 per annum plus excellent benefits
Location: Bishop Auckland Supported Accommodation Service and Tow Law Dispersed Accommodation Service, County Durham
Hours: Full time, 37.5 hours per week
Contract: Permanent, multiple vacancies
Closing date: 17 November 2026

About the Role

Join Depaul UK's supportive team and make a lasting difference to young people experiencing homelessness and other challenges.

We have opportunities for both Young People Support Workers and Night Young People Support Workers across our Bishop Auckland and Tow Law services.

In the day role, you will provide practical and emotional support to help young people develop independent living skills and work towards their goals. In the night role, you will help maintain a safe, welcoming and supportive environment overnight.

Your key responsibilities will include:

Building positive, trusting relationships and delivering tailored, person-centred support.

Completing risk and needs assessments and developing outcomes-based support plans.

Supporting young people to access education, training, employment and volunteering.

Delivering individual and group activities that build confidence, resilience and independence.

Working with colleagues and partner agencies to support wellbeing and safeguarding.

Helping young people settle into their accommodation and involving them in decisions about their support.

Maintaining a safe environment through regular checks and appropriate reporting.

Rotas may include unsocial hours and weekend working.

Please clearly state which role you are applying for and your preferred service location in your application or supporting statement.

About You

You will bring experience of working with young people or people who have experienced homelessness, alongside an understanding of needs relating to mental health and substance misuse.

You will also have:

Knowledge of risk assessments, support planning and safeguarding procedures.

Strong communication, relationship-building and collaborative working skills.

Good literacy, numeracy and IT skills.

A resilient, reflective approach and the ability to maintain professional boundaries.

A commitment to equality, diversity and treating everyone with dignity and respect.
